To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have determined the interaction network between the periplasmically located chaperone Sur A and the transmembrane β-barrel assembly machinery BAM complex, which consists of Bam A and Bam B.

the interaction network between the subunits of BAM and SurA, as revealed by our experimental data and the theoretical structures, is consistent with a mechanism of action in which SurA is the first to interact with the BAM complex, and the latter, in turn, is able to bind to a substrate OMP.
the SurA BAM interaction network is mediated by a conserved surface of SurA, and that this interaction is essential for the proper function of the BAM complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the transmembranal OMP assembly complex.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying the formation of the transmembranous supercomplex, which is responsible for the assembly of OMPs.
the structural and functional aspects of the transmembranal supercomplex involved in OMP biogenesis in Gram negative bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SurA BAM ternary complex is the functional unit that mediates the biogenesis of the OMPs, and that this unit is the active part of the trans-membrane supercomplex.
the SurA BAM complexes are the building blocks of the transmembranal OMP supercomplex, which is activated by a circular conformation change, as proposed in a recent publication.
SurA interacts with BamA and BamB and that the SurA BAM ternary complex is a key player in the biogenesis process of OMPs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

SurA, the chaperone involved in the early steps of the biogenesis pathway of OMPs, interacts with the BAM complex, and the SurA-BAM complex is part of the larger transmembrane super complex involved in the biogeneses of OMPs.
the SurA-BAM complex is a ternary complex with the chaperone binding to the periplasm side of the BAM complex and that the chaperone induces a circular conformation of the complex.

SurA interacts with the transmembrane domain of BamA, which induces a circular conformation in the latter, which in turn induces a conformational change in BamB, which in turn triggers a conformational transition in SurA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SurA BAM ternary complex can adopt two conformations, one of them being the same as that of the SurA BAM binary complex, and the other being different.
the SurA BAM complexes can be considered as an assembly intermediate in the formation of the transmembranesupercomplex.

SurA, a chaperone, is not a mere passive player in the process of OMPs assembly, but it is actively involved in the process, and its presence is required for the proper assembly of the transmembranal supercomplex.
